paragraphs: A big strike in Ireland will not happen. Unions and the Government agreed a new pay deal early on Wednesday.
More than 300,000 public workers planned to stop work on Thursday. Many of them are nurses, teachers and office staff.
The talks went on all night in Dublin. The deal came at about 3.30am.
Workers will get 10.75% more pay. The rises will come in small steps over 33 months. Workers with low pay will get bigger rises.
Last week, the unions said no to a smaller offer of 7.75%. The new deal will cost the State about €5 billion.
Union leaders still need to say a final yes. But most people think this will be easy.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭一場大罷工將不會發生。
工會和政府在星期三清晨達成新的薪資協議。
超過三十萬名公部門員工原本打算在星期四停工。
他們當中很多人是護理師、老師和辦公室職員。
談判在都柏林進行了一整夜。
協議大約在凌晨三點半達成。
員工的薪水將增加10.75%。
加薪會在33個月內分成小步驟進行。
低薪員工會得到較大的加幅。
上星期，工會拒絕了7.75%這個較低的方案。
新協議將花費國家約50億歐元。
工會領袖仍需作出最後的同意。
不過大多數人認為這會很順利。

paragraphs: A national strike planned for Thursday has been called off after unions and the Government agreed a new pay deal in the early hours of Wednesday morning.
The talks took place at the Workplace Relations Commission in Ballsbridge, Dublin. They went on through the night, and the agreement was announced to reporters just after 3.30am.

Under the deal, pay for more than 400,000 public servants will rise by 10.75% over 33 months. The rises will come in stages. Workers on lower pay will get bigger percentage increases, and part of the money will be paid back to an earlier date.

Just over a week ago, the unions rejected an offer of 7.75%. They then planned a one-day strike involving more than 300,000 workers, including staff in hospitals, schools and Government offices. The Government says its new offer will cost about €5 billion. Some health staff would have kept working during the strike.
The unions had also planned large marches in eight cities and towns. About 50,000 members had signed up to take part, including 20,000 in Dublin. Those plans have now been dropped.
Union leaders must still talk to the other unions in the group before the strike is officially cancelled. However, this is expected to be a simple step.
The deal is good news for the Government, as Dublin is hosting a large meeting of European leaders on Thursday.
sentZh: 原定星期四舉行的全國罷工已經取消，因為工會和政府在星期三凌晨達成新的薪資協議。
談判在都柏林Ballsbridge的勞資關係委員會進行。
談判持續了一整夜，協議在凌晨三點半剛過時向記者宣布。
根據協議，超過四十萬名公務員的薪水將在33個月內上漲10.75%。
加薪將分階段進行。
低薪員工會獲得較高的百分比加幅，而部分款項會追溯到較早的日期發放。
一個多星期前，工會拒絕了7.75%的方案。
他們隨後計畫發動一場超過三十萬名員工參與的一日罷工，包括醫院、學校和政府機關的職員。
政府表示新方案將花費約50億歐元。
部分醫療人員在罷工期間仍會繼續工作。
工會也曾計畫在八個城鎮舉行大型遊行。
約有五萬名會員報名參加，其中兩萬人在都柏林。
這些計畫現在已經取消。
在罷工正式取消之前，工會領袖仍須與同一組織內的其他工會商量。
不過，這預計只是一個簡單的步驟。
這項協議對政府來說是好消息，因為都柏林星期四將舉辦一場歐洲領袖的大型會議。

paragraphs: A 24-hour public sector strike due to take place on Thursday has been called off after unions and the Government reached a pay agreement following talks that ran late into the night.

The deal was announced at the Workplace Relations Commission in Ballsbridge shortly after 3.30am on Wednesday. The negotiations had been guided by a Government-appointed steering group chaired by Kevin Foley, the head of the commission.

Under the agreement, wages for more than 400,000 public and civil servants will increase by 10.75% over 33 months. This includes basic rises of at least 7.75%, plus a further 1% linked to local bargaining. Lower-paid staff will receive higher percentage increases, and the first 2% rise will be backdated.

The breakthrough comes just over a week after unions voted to reject an earlier offer worth 7.75%. That decision led to plans for a stoppage involving more than 300,000 workers. The Government has estimated that the improved pay package will cost around €5 billion.

Before the deal, unions had been preparing for a major show of strength. Fórsa said roughly 50,000 members had registered for rallies in eight cities and towns, while Siptu had arranged cover for essential health services.

Full details of the agreement have not yet been published. Union negotiators must first consult the other members of the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions, although formally cancelling the strike is expected to be a formality.
The timing is a relief for the Government, which is hosting the largest-ever gathering of national leaders in Ireland as EU summits take place in Dublin this week.
sentZh: 原定星期四舉行的24小時公部門罷工已經取消，因為工會和政府在談判持續到深夜後達成了薪資協議。
協議於星期三凌晨三點半過後不久在Ballsbridge的勞資關係委員會宣布。
談判由政府任命、委員會主席Kevin Foley主持的指導小組引導。
根據協議，超過四十萬名公務員和文職人員的薪資將在33個月內增加10.75%。
這包括至少7.75%的基本加薪，另加與地方協商掛鉤的1%。
低薪員工將獲得較高的百分比加幅，而第一筆2%的加薪將追溯發放。
這項突破出現在工會投票否決早先價值7.75%的方案僅一個多星期之後。
那個決定導致了超過三十萬名員工參與停工的計畫。
政府估計，改善後的薪資方案將花費約50億歐元。
在協議達成前，工會一直在準備大規模展示實力。
Fórsa表示約有五萬名會員報名參加在八個城鎮舉行的集會，而Siptu則已為必要的醫療服務安排了人手。
協議的完整細節尚未公布。
工會談判代表必須先諮詢愛爾蘭工會大會公共服務委員會的其他成員，不過正式取消罷工預計只是形式上的手續。
這個時機讓政府鬆了一口氣，因為本週歐盟高峰會在都柏林舉行，政府正主辦愛爾蘭有史以來規模最大的國家領袖聚會。

paragraphs: A day-long stoppage across the public sector, scheduled for Thursday, has been averted after unions and the Government struck a pay accord in the small hours of Wednesday morning, following marathon negotiations.

The breakthrough was unveiled to waiting reporters at the Workplace Relations Commission in Ballsbridge shortly after 3.30am. The talks had been steered by a Government-appointed group chaired by Kevin Foley, who heads the commission.

The settlement will lift pay for upwards of 400,000 public and civil servants by 10.75% over 33 months. Basic increases of no less than 7.75% are complemented by a further 1% tied to local bargaining, while the lowest earners stand to gain proportionately more. An initial 2% rise will also be applied retrospectively.

The accord marks a striking turnaround: barely a week earlier, unions had spurned a 7.75% offer, paving the way for a walkout by more than 300,000 workers. Ministers have put the cost of the sweetened package at roughly €5 billion.

Unions had been gearing up for a formidable display of solidarity. Fórsa reported that some 50,000 members had signed up for marches in eight urban centres, and Siptu had secured exemptions so that critical health staff would remain at their posts.

The fine print has yet to be made public, and negotiators must still canvass the remaining affiliates on the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions. Nonetheless, the formal stand-down of the strike is widely regarded as a foregone conclusion.

For the Government, the deal could scarcely have come at a better moment, with Dublin playing host this week to EU summits that will bring together more national leaders than Ireland has ever welcomed.
sentZh: 原定星期四舉行、遍及公部門的全日停工已被化解，因為工會和政府在馬拉松式談判後，於星期三凌晨達成了薪資協議。
這項突破於凌晨三點半過後不久，在Ballsbridge的勞資關係委員會向等候的記者公布。
談判由政府任命、委員會首長Kevin Foley主持的小組主導。
這項協議將使超過四十萬名公務員和文職人員的薪資在33個月內提高10.75%。
不低於7.75%的基本加薪之外，另有與地方協商掛鉤的1%，而收入最低者將按比例獲得更多。
最初的2%加薪也將追溯適用。
這項協議標誌著驚人的轉折：僅僅一週前，工會還拒絕了7.75%的方案，為超過三十萬名員工的罷工鋪了路。
部長們估計這個加碼方案的成本約為50億歐元。
工會原本正準備展現強大的團結。
Fórsa表示約有五萬名會員報名參加在八個城市中心舉行的遊行，而Siptu也已取得豁免，讓關鍵醫療人員能堅守崗位。
細節尚未公開，談判代表仍須徵詢愛爾蘭工會大會公共服務委員會中其餘成員工會的意見。
儘管如此，正式撤銷罷工普遍被視為定局。
對政府而言，這項協議來得正是時候，因為都柏林本週主辦歐盟高峰會，聚集的國家領袖人數將是愛爾蘭有史以來最多的。

paragraphs: A nationwide 24-hour public sector strike, scheduled for Thursday, has been averted following protracted overnight negotiations that culminated in a pay agreement between unions and the Government in the early hours of Wednesday.

The agreement was announced at the Workplace Relations Commission in Ballsbridge shortly after 3.30am. The process had been facilitated by a steering group appointed by the Government and chaired by Kevin Foley, the commission's head.

The settlement provides for a cumulative increase of 10.75% in the remuneration of over 400,000 public and civil servants over a 33-month period. This comprises basic increases of at least 7.75%, supplemented by an additional 1% contingent upon local bargaining. Furthermore, lower-paid employees will receive proportionately larger increases, and an initial 2% rise will be applied retrospectively.

This outcome represents a substantial shift in position, given that unions had rejected a 7.75% offer only a week earlier, consequently precipitating plans for industrial action involving more than 300,000 workers. The Government estimates that the revised package will entail expenditure of approximately €5 billion.

Prior to the agreement, unions had been mobilising on a considerable scale. Fórsa indicated that approximately 50,000 members had registered for demonstrations in eight urban centres, while Siptu had negotiated exemptions to ensure the continuity of essential health services.

The comprehensive terms have not yet been published, and negotiators are obliged to consult the remaining affiliates of the public services committee of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions. Nevertheless, the formal cancellation of the strike is anticipated to be a mere formality.
The timing is particularly advantageous for the Government, as Dublin is simultaneously hosting EU summits that constitute the largest assembly of national leaders in the history of the State.
